Review article

Efficacy on sleep parameters and tolerability of melatonin in individuals
with sleep or mental disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis

Matthew Salanitro a, Torsten Wrigley b, Hisham Ghabra b, Edward de Haan c,d,
Catherine M. Hill e,f, Marco Solmi g,h,i,j, Samuele Cortese j,k,l,m,n,*

ARTICLE INFO        ABSTRACT

Keywords:           We conducted the first systematic review and series of meta-analyses to assess the efficacy and tolerability of
Melatonin           melatonin in children/adolescents or adults with sleep or mental health disorders, using the same set of criteria
Sleep               across disorders and ages. Based on a pre-registered protocol (PROPSPERO: CRD42021289827), we searched a
Neurodevelopmental  broad range of electronic databases up to 02.02.2021 for randomized control trials (RCTs) of melatonin. We
ADHD                assessed study quality using the Risk of Bias tool, v2. We included a total of 34 RCTs (21 in children/adolescents:
ASD                 N = 984; 13 in adults: N = 1014). We found evidence that melatonin significantly improved sleep onset latency
                    and total sleep time, but not sleep awaking, in children and adolescents with a variety of neurodevelopmental
                    disorders, and sleep onset latency (measured by diary) as well as total sleep time (measured with poly
                    somnography) in adults with delayed sleep phase disorder. No evidence of significant differences between
                    melatonin and placebo was found in terms of tolerability. We discuss clinical and research implications of our
                    findings.
